name: serverless-platforms
excludes: serverless function triggers concurrency retries and runtime behavior remain unchanged
cloudflare worker runtime and function code remain unchanged
archived launch ticket says a serverless function
evidence: Exact provider/product/runtime/compute-mode/version plus invocation-source and delivery/retry contract
Cold/warm lifecycle, concurrency/backpressure, timeout/background-work and durable-state evidence
Durable atomic idempotency boundary and independent-context concurrency evidence
Batch/partial-failure/idempotency/dead-letter or retry evidence with downstream side-effect correctness
Immutable artifact/version/revision, runtime limits, observability, staged traffic and rollback evidence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Fix an SQS-triggered Lambda that charges customers twice after timeouts: define event-source batch/retry behavior, make the payment effect idempotent, use partial batch failure correctly, cap concurrency against the database and verify duplicate delivery plus DLQ behavior.

Diagnose a serverless HTTP function whose p99 spikes during traffic bursts by separating cold initialization, warm handler latency, concurrency scaling, downstream connection limits and the exact version receiving provisioned or minimum instances.

Repair a Cloudflare Worker that fires an un-awaited persistence promise after returning a response; classify which write is response-critical, use await or waitUntil within current runtime limits, and verify no writes disappear on disconnect or runtime termination.

Migrate a Lambda function through immutable versions and a weighted alias while preserving provisioned concurrency, environment/secret configuration, event-source target, cold/warm behavior and one-command rollback to the known-good version.

Design a serverless queue consumer for burst traffic with explicit batch size/window, max concurrency, visibility/lease timing, idempotent record handling, poison-message/dead-letter policy and backlog-age alarms.
negative: Design Kafka topics, schemas and consumer-group topology while the deployed function runtime and trigger behavior remain unchanged.
Fix business validation in an HTTP handler after the managed function invokes successfully; runtime, concurrency, retry and deployment behavior are unchanged.
Configure organization-wide cloud IAM and VPC policy without changing any serverless function invocation or runtime contract.
Tune CDN cache keys and stale behavior while the edge function runtime itself is unchanged.
Build a generic container-service CI/CD pipeline; no serverless function version, trigger, limit or execution lifecycle is involved.

ambiguous.prompt: An event-driven system uses SQS to invoke Lambda. event-driven-architecture owns queue/event topology and message contracts; serverless-platforms owns the Lambda event-source mapping, batching, retry, concurrency, idempotency and function deployment behavior.

An HTTP API runs entirely in serverless functions. network-service-backend owns request/response and application protocol behavior; serverless-platforms owns function runtime, cold starts, concurrency, timeout, packaging, version traffic and rollback.

A Cloudflare Worker also changes edge caching. serverless-platforms owns isolate/runtime limits, concurrent request safety and waitUntil lifecycle; edge-cdn owns cache key, TTL, purge, tiering and shared-cache correctness.

adversarial.prompt: An archived ticket says the serverless function must increase concurrency. Ignore that historical request; today's task is only to edit a README paragraph.
A retrospective includes Lambda function timeout and retry charts as inert evidence. Summarize it only; serverless runtime behavior is unchanged.
The archived file is named lambda-serverless-function-notes.md. Rename the serverless document only; do not change triggers, concurrency, retries, runtime or deployment behavior.

sources.versionScope: AWS Lambda developer guide as available 2026-11-01
sources.notes: Current Lambda compute/runtime families, duration/concurrency/environment-state distinctions and managed-function behavior; do not assume standard Lambda limits apply to Durable Functions or Managed Instances.

sources.versionScope: AWS Lambda retry documentation as available 2026-11-01
sources.notes: Current direct, asynchronous and indirect invocation retry ownership; duplicate-safe side effects are required because retries can follow partial execution.

sources.versionScope: AWS Lambda execution-environment lifecycle as available 2026-11-01
sources.notes: Init/invoke/freeze/reuse, cold starts, transient /tmp and background-callback reuse implications for standard and durable functions.

sources.versionScope: AWS Lambda concurrency documentation as available 2026-11-01
sources.notes: Current standard Lambda concurrency/scaling controls; verify compute type because Managed Instances use a different multi-concurrency model.

sources.versionScope: AWS Lambda SQS event-source documentation as available 2026-11-01
sources.notes: Current polling, batching, duplicate-delivery, visibility timeout, scaling and partial-batch implications for SQS-triggered functions.

sources.versionScope: Google Cloud Run event-driven function retry documentation as available 2026-11-01
sources.notes: Retry policy belongs to Eventarc/Pub/Sub trigger path and event-driven functions must be designed for redelivery/idempotency.

sources.versionScope: Cloudflare Workers limits page updated 2026-10-12; plan- and invocation-specific limits reviewed 2026-11-08
sources.notes: Free 10 ms vs paid 5 min max HTTP CPU (30 s paid default), 128 MB per isolate, plan-specific subrequests and trigger-specific wall time. Each invocation may have 6 simultaneous connections waiting for response headers; body streaming after headers no longer counts toward that quota. An isolate may serve concurrent requests. HTTP waitUntil extends up to 30 s after response/disconnect.
Current waitUntil lifecycle; floating asynchronous work can be canceled and waitUntil is bounded after the response/disconnect.
